📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.

According to recent reports, "On November 12th, our board of directors unveiled that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the tech giant's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

According to recent reports, that last bit seems likely to have been remarked with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

Recent findings suggest that "Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the manufacturer navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "latest standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the organization's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

#4935. Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1295 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the tech giant's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors.
  • BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals.
  • Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the tech giant's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it says on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Announced in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

Recent findings suggest that the same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The company grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "currently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

Help: I can't stop obeying traffic laws in GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (839 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A few minutes into my first play session with Grand Theft Auto 6, I was doing my first bit of driving.
  • I immediately floored it, weaving into and out of oncoming traffic and channeling all the years of training in being a vehicular menace I'd been provided by prior Grands Theft Auto.
  • Industry observers note that repeatedly across the hours I've put into GTA 6 since launch, I've been succumbing to an embarrassing habit of obeying driverly etiquette.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A few minutes into my first play session with Grand Theft Auto 6, I was doing my first bit of driving. I'd been cruising down the Leonida Keys, and as I was patiently waiting at a red light and humming along with the radio, I had a sudden realization: I was patiently waiting at a red light.

I immediately floored it, weaving into and out of oncoming traffic and channeling all the years of training in being a vehicular menace I'd been provided by prior Grands Theft Auto. But just a short way down the road, moments after blasting past a few panicked pedestrians I'd aggressively robbed of the right of way, it happened again: Without thinking, I'd come to a complete stop at a stop sign.I'm playing the world's most renowned automotive crime fantasy, and I can't stop observing the basic tenets of road safety.

Industry observers note that repeatedly across the hours I've put into GTA 6 since launch, I've been succumbing to an embarrassing habit of obeying driverly etiquette. I'm following other drivers at a reasonable distance when I could be forcing them off the road to save time. I'm diligently staying in my lane when I could be scraping my way up the shoulder at 90 miles an hour. NPC passengers have berated me mid-mission for not driving fast enough because I'm checking both directions before crossing an intersection. Something is wrong with me.

According to recent reports, to be entirely clear: I've never had this issue before. As with any other sensible person, my time in the two decades and change that I've been playing Grand Theft Auto have been characterized by a blatant disregard for roadway caution. If I was ever driving safely, it was either by accident or as a sort of affectation—like when you do a crappy posh accent to make fun of the moneyed classes.

But in GTA 6, something is different. Something has shifted in the simulation enough that I'm opting out of vehicular psychopathy without even meaning to—something in the increased visual fidelity and the intensified sense of heft and momentum. Something's stepped across some critical line of verisimilitude, and now I'm instinctively treating its virtual cars like the multi-ton slabs of explosion-propelled metal they're meant to evoke.

In a recent development, and it's not just the cars, either. There's a tweet circulating today from a Polish user who noted how firing a weapon in public feels more dire in GTA 6 than in previous entries, demonstrating the point with a video of panicked beachgoers fleeing en masse as Jason fires a pistol into the air. I can confirm that—perhaps not coincidentally—I've been doing a lot less non-vehicular psychopathy, too.

According to recent reports, during in-mission firefights and gang raids, I'm as unphased by the violence on display as I've been by the collective years of videogame combat I've done beforehand. There, it's action movie absurdity. Elsewhere, though, I'm rarely reaching for a firearm. Age is partially to blame: Random acts of simulated violence aren't as titillating at 33 as they were at 12. But the truth is, Rockstar's absurd expenditure of art and animation tech has produced a crime game where firing a gun with no good reason can feel downright criminal.

When there's so much attention dedicated to how characters move and shift their mass, when the world around them is lit so believably and packed with so much detail, the violence you can inflict feels so much more acute. I don't think it's immoral to shoot a gun or drive a car at someone in GTA 6. But I do think it feels queasy—queasy in a way I'm not used to feeling. The uncanny valley isn't latest, but being able to empty a weapon into it is.

#4933. The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1375 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1375 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The “Siri Recap” feature that Apple declared in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on.
  • Industry observers note that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything.
  • Sources indicate that the recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The “Siri Recap” feature that Apple declared in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that debuted at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

Industry observers note that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

Sources indicate that the recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":.

It has been revealed that music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

In a recent development, sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this launched in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

It has been revealed that live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?

I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just said in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

According to recent reports, but Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an enhancement on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel plans, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all.

After you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

Sources indicate that as promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was remarked. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct.

Recent findings suggest that but still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people said to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.).

Industry observers note that because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

When it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

Details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

It has been revealed that but it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

Industry observers note that I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most notable points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

Recent findings suggest that and there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

#4932. Stacey Abrams in Conversation With Ta-Nehisi Coates

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4135 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vanityfair ↗ Open Full Page

Stacey Abrams in Conversation With Ta-Nehisi Coates

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4135 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, when I first met Stacey Abrams in 2015, she passed on to me the message that she was then passing on to anyone who’d listen: Someday soon, Georgia would be blue.
  • The following conversation has been lightly edited for length and clarity.
  • Ta-Nehisi Coates: My recollection of our first meeting goes back to 2015, when I was promoting Between the World and Me.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, when I first met Stacey Abrams in 2015, she passed on to me the message that she was then passing on to anyone who’d listen: Someday soon, Georgia would be blue. This struck me as unlikely. But three years later Abrams ran for governor, and shocked the country by coming within two points of winning. Then two years later, when Joe Biden sealed his presidential election in 2020 with a win in Georgia, and Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff won Senate seats, Abrams looked prophetic. Now, Democrats have gone beyond Georgia, penetrating into the deepest reaches of the South—Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas. To understand how the GOP’s Solid South grew brittle, I could think of no better person to talk to than Abrams.

The following conversation has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Ta-Nehisi Coates: My recollection of our first meeting goes back to 2015, when I was promoting Between the World and Me. You interviewed me for the book. We had a wonderful discussion. My family was actually in the audience, because, like all Black folks, I have family in Atlanta. They were so excited. I was talking to Stacey Abrams—Minority Leader Stacey Abrams. And one of the things you said backstage was, “We’re going to make Georgia blue.” And I don’t know that I scoffed at you. I like to think I wasn’t quite that rude.

Stacey Abrams: Your eyebrow arched a bit.

I confess to the eyebrow arching. And so the eyebrow arched and you made the case. Can you tell me what you saw?

I’d gone through redistricting, and one of the component pieces of redistricting, of course, is that it’s predicated on the census. The US census is a tool that is incredibly powerful and deeply inexact. It was the first time Republicans had power to draw the lines since Reconstruction. And I took a posture in my caucus, and it was this: “If you vote for their maps, I will come after your seats.” And I was not only unequivocal in saying it, I wrote it down because I didn’t want anyone to misquote me.

Recent findings suggest that in order to take that posture, I had to read the maps myself. And what I saw was that Republicans were placing bets that, by drawing the lines a certain way, they were going to give themselves 124 of 180 seats. So 67% of the seats, even though they’d only won the election by 57%.

In a recent development, but I looked at those same maps and I’m like, In this place, in this part of Paulding County, there is a new subdivision that is predominantly Black. And in this part of Gwinnett County, there is a burgeoning Korean population that is now going into its second generation, which means a lot of those will be eligible voters. And down in South Georgia, you have third-generation migrant farm workers who are Latino, but who have decided to plant their roots here and raise their families here. When you looked at those numbers, the maps had a very different story to tell about Republican dominance: They could win for a decade. They could not win for a generation.

In a recent development, we tell ourselves stories about the information we get, and people repeat stories without ever reading it themselves. There are a lot of people who can quote Tom Sawyer who’ve never read the book. And so in our politics, that happens a lot, that the story that becomes popular doesn’t ever get traced back to its origin or to the original text.

According to recent reports, what I saw in Georgia is true in Louisiana, in Mississippi, in Tennessee, in Alabama, in South Carolina. We just saw it happen in North Carolina.

So when you saw this wave of redistricting happening around the country this year, did you see a similar opportunity?

Oh, absolutely. I was in Tennessee the day that they passed the maps and what stuck out for me was Raumesh Akbari, who’s the Senate minority leader, she asked to see the bill, and the Republican chair of the committee noted, “Well, we don’t have a bill yet, but we know what it’s going to say.” They planned to vote on it even though they did not have the text of the bill.

In a recent development, the Republicans were moving so fast because they thought they understood what they were pulling together. Justin Pearson didn’t pick up the seat he wanted, but they were at risk of losing a seat they thought was going to be theirs because they misread the topography, but they didn’t do a deeper dive into exactly what was laying in the crevices. And that’s where opportunity for us is born.

Industry observers note that there are not enough Black people to win any single seat outright on their own in most legislative districts, and no statewide elections, especially post–Louisiana v. Callais, but there are coalitions that can be built. And what I saw from the very beginning was the possibility of coalition.

Industry observers note that what I see for the South, what I think the South proved on Tuesday, is the possibility of coalition, but coalition does not happen without conflict. It does not happen without conversation, and it does not happen when we have convinced ourselves of the permanence of our second-class citizenship and our subjugation. What we saw on Tuesday was a moment where people realized that the power to improve their own lives had become so desperately thin that they had to use it or lose it. We cannot rely on that for the next two years.

According to recent reports, what I hear you saying is that the last two years created an emergency. But that can’t be depended on. It can’t be “The Most Notable Election of Our Lifetime” every two years. Desperation is not enough.

According to recent reports, it can’t be. Desperation gets you one moment. There’s a whole body of medical research on people that have heart attacks and they get saved. And what it highlights is that they are exercise fiends for about six weeks and then they fall back into their patterns because it’s a normalcy bias.

According to recent reports, if we constantly feel on the edge of danger, we cannot function. And so we reorient our understanding of normal to survive. And therefore our responsibility in this moment is to look at the opportunity that was revealed on Tuesday, but not read into it that that opportunity either requires desperation or it requires this milquetoast approach, because our default is not just normalcy, but the most banal form of normalcy we can imagine.

I know you have some concerns about some of the narratives emerging out of the midterms. Would you talk a bit about that?

According to recent reports, I saw something on Axios that I think was well-intentioned and it essentially said that the threats to our democracy were overblown, that our courts held, that our Congress held, that our presidency wasn’t overreaching, and that for normal people, things were fine. How have we reached the place where we think it is normal that the capital city in the United States of America is under military occupation? How is it okay that the courts held when it permits the incarceration of children in Dilley, Texas, and the kidnapping of people of color because of race and the language that they speak? There is something aggressively privileged about this idea that democracy is not in jeopardy because those who are the most protected don’t feel harm.

In a recent development, but Tuesday was a repudiation of this idea that things are normal. You saw turnout at extraordinary levels from a cross section of communities, almost all of whom have been directly impacted by the harms of this administration. Not just the economic harms that hit everyone, but harms that were amplified and refined for their cruelty.

At the same time, there’s a worry that I have that, because we won control of Congress for the patriots—and that’s how I frame it, I no longer think it’s just Democrat versus Republican, it’s patriots versus authoritarians—even though the patriots may have gained more purchase in Congress, we still have a Supreme Court that gutted the last vestiges of protection for the Voting Rights Act. We still have a Supreme Court that stripped women of their bodily autonomy. We still have a Supreme Court that has noted that protections that are afforded by DEI are somehow suspect. And when those are true, then the successes of Tuesday don’t signal that we’ve won. They signal that we have to work even harder because the harms have not dissipated, they just haven’t penetrated.

You noted something a few months back that’s stuck with me—that our elections are ripe for entertainment. As a sports fan, I think it’s not a coincidence that so many sports figures are now commenting on politics because the way they appear on TV is actually quite similar to the way sports appears. You have these long campaigns, which is like your season. Then you have primaries, which are like your playoffs, and then you have this big Super Bowl that happens on Tuesday. And so, it’s an entertainment and ratings bonanza. And I think, as I recall, you were cautioning against that as a view of politics. Can you speak a little bit more about that?

Yeah. When you think about politics, if you think about elections as an event, and to extend your analogy, if the elections are the finals, if the elections are game seven, if it’s the Super Bowl, when that happens, then the day after, you go home, the game is over. But the challenge I have is that it’s not just that we treat it as a sporting event, it’s that we treat politics as though we are spectators at a sporting event. And when we look at the other party, it’s like we are spectators watching a very disciplined, seasoned team that practices in the off-season, that travels together, that plays overseas. They’re constantly engaged and we are on and off. We think of politics, again, as entertainment as opposed to the job.

How did we end up with this entertainment narrative?

Sources indicate that theodore White did this series where he examined elections 1960, 1964, 1968, 1972. And when you read it, as someone who is reading it in the 21st century, the arc of how we have viewed politics changed dramatically, specifically in 1960 with the advent of television, because the election contest between John Kennedy and Richard Nixon hinged in no small part on that televised debate. And I think for you and me and for anyone who wasn’t old enough to see it, I did not realize that it was one of the most watched programs in American history. We take for granted how many people are going to watch the debates these days, but with that first debate, it was one of the most watched programs in the world because it had never happened before. And the moment it became a television spectacle, it became entertainment because you were watching, you picked winners and losers, you picked your villain and you picked your champion.

It has been revealed that it’s human nature, we put things into these narrative arcs. As someone who writes comic books, you understand this. As someone who writes thrillers, I think about this. You create a villain, you have a protagonist, an antagonist, you have to have a storyline, you have to have complications, and when television became the medium, it added a layer and a texture to what had long been the mechanics of politics. Then you add into it the drama of Black and brown people getting to participate. And then you layer on top of that “blue state versus red state,” and the sharp division, and the attribution to entire regions of a value system and a personality based on a single day.

What would it mean to remain engaged beyond elections? When I think about the conservative movement, I think about the degree to which the religious right is engaged. I think about Trump rallies. I think people were baffled by this at first—the clothes, the trucks, the boats. But what I would say is those are markers of community. They aren’t my politics. But they seem part of something larger than a particular bill or policy.

There’s a lot of talk in organizing about going for belief first, or belonging first. On the left, we are often accused of belief, that you have to be in line with all of our ideas, our values, our ideologies, but also the tactical, practical ways of exercising them, and that because we say you have to believe first, we filter out people who haven’t had time to understand or adapt or even decide what they believe. The right uses belonging. They say, “Come and be a part of us, and we’ll tell you what we are.” So you get the jersey, you get the cap, you get the red, you get to use the language, even if you haven’t decided that you actually believe all they believe, which is why you have people who are suddenly surprised that this is what happened.

Recent findings suggest that we have to shift. Not to say that we don’t have beliefs, but we have to give people time to grow into those beliefs. I come at this from my time as minority leader. I had a caucus of 60 members in a chamber of 180, and my members included suburban white mothers and rural Black pastors and everything in between. We were the most racially diverse caucus. We were geographically diverse. And I had no power. I was the minority leader. My job was to help harmonize their approach. I could not lead with belief, because people were entitled to their beliefs, but my job was to bring them into belonging first because they were members of the caucus. And then my second job was to make sure that anyone who needed them to believe something had the platform to offer the tutelage.

That’s the place where I think we are failing. We don’t do the tutelage. We say, “There has been a conversation, this is now our truth. And if you don’t adopt that truth, you are somehow opposed to it,” as opposed to, “You haven’t adopted the truth because you don’t know what it means and you don’t understand it and you haven’t experienced it. Let me give you time and space to come in,” or, “You have legitimate disagreement, and maybe on this, we will not be in alignment, but your disagreement should not lead to hostility against my community.”.

The Democratic Socialists of America have attracted a lot of attention recently, but one thing they seem to do is this “belonging” piece. I can’t say I understood this before, but I was talking to someone for a story, and then mentioned the social environment. So here in Upcoming York, when people go out to canvas, afterwards, they all go out for beers. The beers are not really the point, but making people feel like they belong to something is.

Recent findings suggest that yeah. I mean, what they are doing is what works in most effective social movements. During the Vietnam War, one of the most effective protest waves happened at coffee shops. You brought people together around the table, they got to vent about what they were upset about, they went out and protested and then they came back together. People like being liked.

According to recent reports, in terms of belief, how does one do that and not make those who are in that coalition who are particularly vulnerable feel abandoned? Obviously, I mean, this is not the only case, but I’m thinking about the tremendous amount of negative attention brought on the trans community. What do you do when the “belonging” comes in conflict with actually protecting the members of your coalition?

Industry observers note that my first position is, if you have a faith that tells you it is okay to cause harm because you feel uncomfortable, I need to understand where your faith lies. Our first responsibility is the protection of difference. And it is to say you don’t have to embrace, but you cannot lift up pitchforks. You cannot demonize, you cannot revile, you cannot scapegoat because all of those are hostile actions of cruelty that not only cause harm to the victim, they diminish your ability to learn. So the worry I have is that too often we sacrifice that education piece because it’s uncomfortable and because it requires defending those you may not be in complete alignment with, and it’s an easier thing to just jump on the bandwagon.

In a recent development, in my caucus, when I was a minority leader, another issue I had was abortion, and I had two members who were pastors. I was not going to be able to change their ideological position and I wasn’t going to try. But I had these members walk off the floor, instead of voting, on abortion bills. And there were some who got mad and they’re like, “Oh, we should know their position.” I stated, “A yes vote on this bill causes harm, and no vote is a help. Not voting is the same as a no vote. So why do you need them to make a declaration when their declaration of refusing to do harm is progress?” So there’s a complexity that we often elide because we failed to measure what harm looks like, and the path from good to harm is a lot shorter than we want to believe.

Did you work with Angie Nixon during her race?

I feel like she excited a certain element of the base in a way that we haven’t really seen before.

In a recent development, I contributed and then I went down to Florida, actually did an event at Florida A&M University and did one at Cafe Resistance. I got to know her mama. I knew of her as a state representative. And when I decided to support her campaign, it was because she has always put the work of serving people first. She has built networks, but more importantly, she solves problems.

Industry observers note that when Florida started banning books, she started a bookstore for banned books. That kind of tactical response with strategic intention is often lacking and it has been part of how I try to operate. We’ve got people who are good at being diagnosticians and we’ve got folks who can offer prescriptions and we’ve got people who can actually administer the medicine. And we need more people who are willing to do all three. You need people who are specialists; I’m not saying you don’t, but what she has demonstrated is the capacity to do the three.

Have you heard some of the negative commentary after the election about her campaign? I’m thinking about James Carville, for instance—this notion that somehow she was a poor fit for Florida or was a bad candidate. It’s not great. Have you seen any of this?

I have. I don’t read very much of it.

Well, I have thoughts on the fact that we keep thinking the solution to the problem is the thing that failed before. And I believe in experimentation. If you look at my history, I have never been top of mind as the solution to problems. And some of it is timing, some of it is capacity, and some of it is helping change the public imagination, but we’re never going to get what we need if we only use what we’ve always had.

I just find it interesting that she is attracting negative commentary, from certain quarters, in a way that David Jolly is not, even though they both lost and the margin wasn’t that much between the two of them. She came very, very close to winning, in a state Democrats really didn’t expect to compete in two years ago. And look, I just have to say, you are somebody who in 2018 came really, really close too. You’re both Black women. I just wonder what you make of the critique.

Sources indicate that the critique is easy because Angie Nixon is different. She’s different than what they are used to, and she is different than 250 years of expectation has led us to presume is right. I am excited about Juliana Stratton and Angela Alsobrooks and Lisa Blunt Rochester being in the US Senate. That is an extraordinary thing. Adding Angie Nixon would’ve been an amazing, amazing addition. But for pundits whose sense of success is grounded in past history, she strains the imagination.

According to recent reports, david Jolly ran a smart race. Angie Nixon ran a smart race, and we know that because they came close to winning, but you are never entitled to victory. You are entitled to effort. And this notion that there is some magical formula for what wins in the South got completely obliterated yesterday when Scott Colom won a seat that we haven’t held since 1874. We know that what can win is a combination of a smart candidate, an invested campaign, and an electorate who sees and hears themselves in the story told.

Angie didn’t get that opportunity because she had a late primary and no resources. And to judge her using a metric that was never designed for her is deeply problematic. And it’s not just about her being a Black woman, it’s about how do we win an evolving electorate if all we know is to do what we’ve always done? And so my argument for the Democratic Party is that our notions of electability have to evolve with the democracy that we deserve and that we design, and it cannot be anchored to these sometimes antiquated notions that the only thing we can do is not lose as opposed to let’s try really hard to win by meeting the moment. And I think Angie Nixon did an incredible job of meeting the moment.

And what about you—do you still have ambitions for public office?

Do you worry that some of the work you do as a kind of public political strategist (like in this interview, frankly) will conflict at all? When I think about people seeking office, they often try to say as little as possible.

It has been revealed that politics is a tool. It is not an identity for me. It’s a tool. And that’s different. And there are people for whom this is what they do and we need those people. This is not a disparaging comment about others, but for me, it is a tool. It is one of the ways to do the work I believe needs to be done. I think that poverty is immoral. I think it is solvable. I think it is economically inefficient. And for most of my life, the work for me has been about how do you solve this economic poverty? When I got deep in the work, I realized that we also had a moral poverty that we had to contend with, and we have this poverty of imagination. And the problem is you cannot convince people to believe that their problems can be solved if you won’t talk about them.

It has been revealed that and in the South, silence is protective. It has been a way to nibble around the edges, but the only people who could be loud about it were the people who could afford volume. And politicians rarely can afford volume. I want things to be better and I’m not willing to forgo any tool that will make that happen. But I’m also not willing to protect my future opportunities by rejecting my current responsibilities.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware.
  • The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.
  • Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

Sources indicate that "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

VisionQuest showrunner Terry Matalas has confirmed Jim Hammond fought in World War 2, alongside Steve Rogers' Captain America.

It has been revealed that jim Hammond finally made his MCU debut in the Disney Plus show, though his costume could first be glimpsed in Captain America: The First Avenger, way back in 2011. He was created by Phineas Horton.

According to recent reports, "I think he was doing exactly that," Matalas shared in an interview, when asked if Hammond fought Nazis or saved people in London. "I think he was part of the Invaders. Latest Update: 10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (858 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit.
  • It has been revealed that reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private.
  • Recent findings suggest that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

It has been revealed that reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Recent findings suggest that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access.

Industry observers note that many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

Industry observers note that A multireddit is a feed that shows posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in upcoming Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

In a recent development, if you want to reduce Reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

Reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by latest, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

Sources indicate that after all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

If you’re playing GTA 6 and finding it too dark, there’s a good chance you may have your HDR calibration wrong – and no, it’s not your fault!

An extensive research video by HDTV Test – performed on a pricey Sony reference monitor – reveals the game’s HDR calibration may not be working quite as intended.

So while you may have followed the steps perfectly, setting your values until the Rockstar logo is only just visible as instructed, it may not be displaying optimally in your game.

I’d recommend you watch HDTV Test’s video for the full scientific analysis, but in short he explains that the various values in the HDR calibration settings output unexpectedly in-game.

Furthermore, the Rockstar release completely ignores Sony’s global PS5 HDR settings, so while you may have those calibrated perfectly for your particular screen, that won’t help you here.

Here’s how to fix it on PS5, according to HDTV Test – although do keep in mind your optimal personal settings will depend on your display, room, and preferred ambient lighting.

Load the game and press Options > Settings > Display > HDR Calibration.

HDTV Test recommends ignoring Rockstar’s own brightness calibration, so don’t worry too much if the organization’s iconic logo is visible or not.

Instead focus on the two sample images of the party on the boat, which you can toggle between light and dark using R1.

These are the recommended starting settings for a display capable of 1,000 nits or higher:.

Feel free to tune these to taste; your own optimal HDR calibration settings will depend on your environment and screen, after all.

But this should help with the overall appearance of the game, and ensure you’re able to see a little bit better in the dark.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games.
  • Recent findings suggest that in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time.
  • In a recent development, the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a newly introduced developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

Recent findings suggest that in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

In a recent development, the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

Recent findings suggest that raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the new team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

Everything You Missed at Vanity Fair's Screening Room Los Angeles

  • Not even a nationwide FAA ground stop could prevent movie stars from descending upon Los Angeles for the Governor Awards and Vanity Fair's first annual Screening Room this past weekend.
  • The weekend began with a screening of Wild Horse Nine, director Martin McDonagh's dark comedy starring John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as CIA agents behind the initiative to overthrow the Chilean government in 1973.
  • It has been revealed that next up was Elsinore, which tells the story of Scottish actor Ian Charleson (played by Andrew Scott) who attempts to perform Hamlet at the National Theatre while secretly living with AIDS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Not even a nationwide FAA ground stop could prevent movie stars from descending upon Los Angeles for the Governor Awards and Vanity Fair's first annual Screening Room this past weekend. Hosted at LACMA's brand-latest Steve Tisch theater, actors including Matt Damon, Penélope Cruz, Pedro Pascal, Andrew Garfield, John Leguizamo, and Andrew Scott joined Q&As to discuss their films and pressing topics in the entertainment industry. AI was a major theme throughout the weekend, and not just at the screening for Artificial, as actors and directors spoke about the desire to continue making things that feel “real” and “made by humans.” Following each screening, talent mingled with guests to continue the conversations.

The weekend began with a screening of Wild Horse Nine, director Martin McDonagh's dark comedy starring John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as CIA agents behind the initiative to overthrow the Chilean government in 1973. Following the showing, VF's Senior Hollywood Correspondent Rebecca Ford led a Q&A with McDonagh, Malkovich and Mariana di Girolamo, who also stars in the film.

It has been revealed that next up was Elsinore, which tells the story of Scottish actor Ian Charleson (played by Andrew Scott) who attempts to perform Hamlet at the National Theatre while secretly living with AIDS. In conversation with VF's Rebecca Ford, Scott, his costar Billie Piper, and writer Stephen Beresford, Scott discussed what it was like to tell Charleson's story. “I think … why the film is so moving is because [Charleson’s] not wallowing at any point. He was insanely courageous,” he mentioned.

It has been revealed that come Friday night, audiences gathered for a screening of the acclaimed Spanish language drama La Bola Negra, which follows several gay men whose lives are bound together by their identities, love and loss, and the looming presence of the Spanish Civil War. It stars Miguel Bernardeau, Álvaro Lafuente Calvo (the singer known as Guitarricadelafuente) in his first major acting role, Carlos Gonzalez, Milo Quifes and Penélope Cruz.

It has been revealed that after the film, Ricky Martin moderated a panel conversation featuring directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, and stars Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente and Bernardeau. Calvo talked about how they are all riding high on the film's positive reception. “Creating this sense of community and hearing people saying, ‘This movie changed me. It really made me understand things about me.’ The power that art has, we forget it, but then this happens and … the rest is a dream. The rest we're living is a dream.”.

Saturday's slate of programming began with a live recording of Vanity Fair's “Notes on a Scene” with Matt Damon, John Leguizamo and Himesh Patel, who recounted what it was like to film The Odyssey with director Christopher Nolan. Next, Seth Rogen joined Screening Room for “Scene Selection,” taking the audience through what it was like shooting Freaks and Geeks, Knocked Up, The Studio and more.

Later that afternoon, Pedro Pascal and Tony Gilroy joined the festivities following a screening of their fresh film Behemoth!, which tells the story of a prodigal cellist who returns to Los Angeles and to score films after decades performing symphonic work around the country. In conversation with VF's West Coast Editor John Ross for Behemoth!, Pascal spoke about how making the film gave him “a tremendous amount of hope.” “We weren't making money on this movie. Nobody was. And you had the most expensive people involved in this film because of their talent and their experience. So there was just this purity of love in the work from every single department, and that was incredibly contagious," he said.

In a recent development, come Saturday night, guests were eager to see Luca Guadagnino's Artificial, which follows the rise of OpenAI and a few of its pioneers: Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever and Mira Murati. Guadagnino was joined by cast members Andrew Garfield (who plays Altman), Yura Borisov (who plays Sutskever) and Monica Barbaro (who plays Murati) for a post-screening conversation with VF's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci. “It's important to try to understand because as Luca remarked, these are the kids that have the reins of the future and we've somehow allowed them to just hold onto them. And we've kind of given our autonomy over or it's been taken from behind our backs,” Garfield said.

On Sunday, Cruz joined director Florian Zeller for a screening of the film Bunker, a timely film about a famous architect, played by Javier Bardem, and his wife Sofia, played by Cruz, who is asked to build a bunker for a tech giant. This sparks a rift in their marriage as the couple examines how success and monetary gain have affected their lives. Cruz, who is having a huge year with The Invite and La Bola Negra alongside this film, expressed her excitement that younger audiences are coming back to theaters and are looking for films that don't “over-explain.".

Industry observers note that the inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room paired this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that included post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

Screening Room is made possible by sponsors Google, CHANEL High Jewelry and Meta VR Glasses.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What do Disney Parks, Make-A-Wish, and the Hallmark Channel all have in common? They love making dreams come true, and that’s exactly what happened for one teenage Hallmark movie superfan who has dreamt about being in one of the cable channel’s movies for a very long time.

Make-A-Wish partnered with Hallmark and Disney to make 14-year-old Ceci’s dreams come true, flying her and her family out to Disney World in Orlando, Florida, to appear in the upcoming Hallmark movie set at a Disney Park. Just like the film’s star Lacey Chabert, Ceci’s day started in the hair and makeup chair as the dedicated artists prepped her for a massive moment. She was then decked out in newly introduced Christmas Disney Parks merch by wardrobe before being taken to set, where she not only got her own chair with her name on it, but also got a chance to meet with the cast of the highly anticipated Hallmark holiday flick.

Both Ceci and her mom got to appear in what is apparently one of the major scenes in the holiday romance film, titled Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True. They can be seen as hotel guests, sitting in the lobby of Disney’s Polynesian Village Resort holding Minnie Mouse and Dumbo plushies. I know I’m definitely going to be keeping my eyes open for the mother-daughter duo when the movie premieres as part of the 2026 TV Schedule on the Hallmark Channel on November 28th at 8 p.m. ET.

The excitement didn’t stop there, though, because Ceci also got a chance to step behind the camera alongside the film’s director. Not only did she get to learn what goes into directing one of Hallmark’s biggest movies yet, but she also got to yell “Action” on set. Watch:.

A post shared by Disney Parks (@disneyparks).

Filming wrapped early this year on what could be Hallmark’s best Countdown to Christmas movie of 2026, but the magic hasn’t stopped for Ceci, who was surprised once again when her entire family was flown back out to Walt Disney World to attend the red-carpet premiere.

Recent findings suggest that as if walking a red carpet as a teenager isn’t exciting enough, she also got to pose alongside the film’s star. I don’t know what I’m more jealous of: the fact that she got to walk the red carpet or that she got to see Chabert in her stunning Disney Princess-inspired gown. Probably both! Ceci stunned as well in a gorgeous burgundy gown that is perfect for the holiday season.

All of this is making me more excited for the film! Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True centers on Lindsey (Chabert), who prepares to spend the holidays at Disney World with her extended family. In addition to having the best holiday ever, Lindsey also makes a wish at Cinderella’s Fountain for a love worthy of a fairytale to find her.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In a recent development, enter Philip (Travis Van Winkle), a man Lindsey went on a disastrous first date with who just so happens to also be spending the holiday with his family at the “Most Magical Place On Earth.” As Lindsey and Philip’s paths continue to cross, sparks start to fly. It seems like Ceci isn’t the only one whose wish is going to be coming true.

Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True premieres first on the Hallmark Channel on November 28th, but will be available to stream the next day on Hallmark+ and Disney+ with an active subscription.

Industry News: SteamDB will add "affiliate links to authorised game retailers" and a new tab dedicated to mods, first upgrade since Nexus Mods takeover confirms

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (728 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a first substantial enhancement since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have announced some additions coming to the community-run backend database.
  • "We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick revision on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.
  • Industry observers note that there are two main upcoming features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a first substantial enhancement since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have announced some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.

"We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick revision on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

Industry observers note that there are two main upcoming features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon. The first is one that anyone could have seen coming, a new tab on each moddable game's page that highlights off some mods hosted for it on Nexus Mods and a host of modding-related data. "The new tab will help you discover mods for games you're browsing on SteamDB, making it easier to see whether a game has an active modding community and explore what it has to offer," Fomann wrote. "For now, we'll only be showing mods from Nexus Mods, as we already have access to that wealth of modding data, making it a straightforward starting point for this new feature.

"We appreciate that some of you might be wondering why we're not including Steam Workshop, too. It's certainly something we'd be open to exploring as we develop the feature further, along with other modding sources. With that in mind, if you run a modding website and would be interested in having your community's mods included, we'd love to hear from you.".

Sources indicate that that seems perfectly fine, but the other incoming feature's a bit more controversial given SteamDB's historically not been all about the money. "One thing we've seen people ask for is an easier way to find the cheapest place to buy a game, and we're now working on making that possible," Folmann wrote. "We'll be introducing affiliate links to authorised game retailers, giving you more options when looking for the best available price on a game.

Sources indicate that "We recognise that introducing affiliate links may raise some concerns, so we want to be clear about how they'll work. First and foremost, as I mentioned, we'll only feature authorised retailers; we will not be including grey-market resellers. We've also made a deliberate decision about how prices are displayed: retailers will be ordered by the cheapest available price in your currency, not by whichever retailer offers us the highest affiliate commission. If a retailer doesn't offer pricing in your currency, we'll still show deals in other currencies provided they are available in your region.".

Folmann was clear in the initial announcement of the takeover that Nexus Mods' bosses would be actively looking into ways SteamDB could make more money to sustain itself, so the addition of these links isn't out of the blue either. Whether SteamDB regulars agree that they're a "lighter-touch" way of earning the site some cash without detracting from the traditional experience of using it is another matter. I'll need to see how I feel once I've actually navigated a few pages with the links in as part of looking up stuff about games, but my first instinct is that as long as the pages don't end up revolving around the links and it's still easy to get to the info you want without interacting with them, I probably won't be too put out.

Beyond those tweaks, Folmann mentioned "improvements to how updates are tested before they go live" and how promptly the team can react to issues have been among the less obvious work going on behind the scenes. "We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve, and there's plenty more work we need to do and would like to work on," he wrote in closing.

Folmann and co only took over Nexus Mods in June last year, making them still relatively new custodians of both it and SteamDB.

Industry News: 10 Hacks Every Hulu User Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations.
  • Recent findings suggest that another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain demonstrates.
  • Industry observers note that if you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations. "Disliking" a show or movie removes it from your Home view and You May Also Like entirely, so the only way you'll see that content is if you search for it. You can dislike on the Details page if you're watching on your TV or use the thumbs down on mobile or web. (The "Like" button will obviously influence your algorithm in the opposite way). If your "Continue Watching" queue is cluttered with indicates you started but didn't like enough to finish, you can remove them from your watch history as well as the My Stuff list. This, too, will allow content to remain searchable but not suggested in other areas of the app.

Recent findings suggest that another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain demonstrates. This keeps content from influencing your recommendations and prevents other viewers from seeing what's in your watch history or saved content (especially if there are things you want to keep private).

Industry observers note that if you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it. Hulu allows you to adjust the color and opacity of the font, background, and window so you get the right contrast, and you can also select the specific font and font scaling. On your streaming device, go to Settings > Subtitles & Captions, then hit the back button on your remote to save your preferences. You can upgrade these settings on mobile and desktop as well.

If you have a long list of shows and films to watch but can't decide what to start next, look for the "Expiring Soon" badge to see which titles are leaving the service in the next two weeks. Badges display the number of days remaining, so you can determine what to prioritize and whether it's worth diving in based on how much time you have to finish before the expiration date. Go to "My Stuff" to monitor saved titles that are expiring soon.

If you've been watching Hulu under an account shared with family or friends and need to switch to your own subscription, you can transfer your profile to keep your watch history and settings intact instead of starting from scratch. You can initiate a profile transfer on a TV-connected device. Note that account holders have to approve transfer requests within seven days, and once expired, transfer requests cannot be resubmitted—so be sure to let the primary user know that you've made the request.

In a recent development, if you've shared your Hulu login information with friends or activated your account on devices you don't own, you may want to regularly audit where your account is being used and remove any that don't need access. This includes TVs in Airbnbs and hotels. If you stay logged in, unauthorized users may have access to your Hulu account and personal data. You can see activated devices (and their activation date) under Your Account > Watch Hulu on Your Devices > Manage Devices. Click Remove next to old or unrecognized devices.

Hulu has an offline mode that allows you to download indicates and movies to watch when you don't have a network connection. This is useful for traveling or when you know your wifi or cell service will be limited. Downloads are only available on supported iOS and Android devices, which means you may have to consider how much space your content takes up. You can select High for video quality if you want maximum resolution, but you may want to choose Standard if you are short on storage. This option is available under Downloads > Settings > Video Quality on iOS and Account > Settings > Downloads > Video Quality on Android. Note that once you click play on downloaded content, you have 48 hours to watch it before it expires—so don't start it unless you are ready.

In a recent development, if you have a Hulu + Live TV subscription, you must designate a "Home" network, which determines the local channels included in your blueprint. You can revision your location up to four times within a 12-month period, but this limitation is meant to prevent viewers outside a household from sharing a subscription. Hulu does allow you to stream live TV on mobile when you're away from your home network (within the U.S.) as long as you access your account on that network every 30 days. If you travel often, check in with your mobile device frequently to avoid being locked out when you're away. Note that you can still watch streaming content with no restrictions.
